metadata.title: The Parisi Formula (Talagrand, 2006)
metadata.framework: Rigorous proof that the Parisi replica symmetry breaking formula exactly computes the free energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Talagrand (2006). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: SK model and free energy
nodes.statement: The Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with Hamiltonian $H_N(\sigma) = \sum_{i<j} g_{ij} \sigma_i \sigma_j / \sqrt{N}$ where $g_{ij}$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian. The quenched free energy per site is $p_N = \frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \log \sum_\sigma \exp(-\beta H_N(\sigma))$. The theorem proves $\lim_{N \to \infty} p_N = \inf_\mu \mathcal{P}(\mu)$.

nodes.name: Parisi functional
nodes.statement: The Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}(\mu)$ is parameterized by a probability measure $\mu$ on $[0,1]$ (equivalently a non-decreasing function $x(q)$ on $[0,1]$). It involves a solution to the Parisi PDE: $\partial_t u = -\frac{1}{2}(u'' + x(t)(u')^2)$ with boundary conditions determined by $\mu$.

nodes.name: Parisi formula (upper bound)
nodes.statement: For the SK model: $\lim_{N \to \infty} p_N \leq \inf_\mu \mathcal{P}(\mu)$. Combined with Guerra's matching lower bound ($p_N \geq \mathcal{P}(\mu)$), this proves $\lim_{N \to \infty} p_N = \inf_\mu \mathcal{P}(\mu)$, confirming the Parisi ansatz.

nodes.name: Proof strategy: cavity method and ultrametricity
nodes.statement: The proof of the upper bound uses: (1) the Aizenman-Sims-Starr cavity method (adding one spin at a time), (2) the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities (constraints on the overlap distribution), (3) ultrametricity of the overlap structure (following from Ghirlanda-Guerra via Panchenko), and (4) construction of Ruelle probability cascades (RPCs) as the natural Gibbs measure structure.

nodes.name: Difficulty relative to Guerra's bound
nodes.statement: Guerra's lower bound is a short, elegant interpolation argument (5 pages). Talagrand's matching upper bound is a 60+ page technical tour de force requiring deep understanding of the Gibbs measure structure. The asymmetry reflects that proving a lower bound on free energy only requires a good trial state, while proving an upper bound requires understanding the full structure.

nodes.name: Resolution of a 25-year-old conjecture
nodes.statement: The Parisi formula was conjectured in 1979-1980 based on the non-rigorous replica trick from statistical physics. The Guerra-Talagrand proof (2003-2006) was the first rigorous confirmation, earning Talagrand recognition including contributions to his Fields Medal considerations.
